blocking: Mobile navigation is unavailable when site.js fails: links remain display:none and the menu button has no native fallback.
The perpetual branch animation has no pause control; the visible pause button controls only video.
Closing the mobile menu with Escape can leave keyboard focus inside the now-hidden navigation.

fixes.what: Keep mobile navigation visible by default; collapse it only after drawer handlers initialize successfully. Hide the toggle until initialization.
fixes.why: Navigation must remain usable when JavaScript fails or is blocked.

fixes.what: When Escape closes an open drawer, return focus to navToggle. Close the drawer when keyboard focus moves outside the header, and reset its state when entering the desktop breakpoint.
fixes.why: Prevents hidden focus and a lingering drawer covering the page during keyboard navigation or resizing.

fixes.where: assets/js/site.js — branch sway and reduced-motion initialization
fixes.what: Provide a pause mechanism for continuous decorative animation, or stop branch sway after a finite introduction. Listen for reduced-motion preference changes and tear down Lenis and motion timelines while restoring visible content.
fixes.why: The video pause button leaves infinite branch motion running, and changing the system preference currently leaves GSAP animations active.

fixes.what: Hide cloud layers by default and reveal them only when their motion timeline is initialized; preserve the unobstructed poster and arch in reduced-motion and dependency-failure modes.
fixes.why: Cloud sources load before the motion guard, but their initial opacity and positioning are established only by GSAP.

fixes.what: At mobile widths, expose all stacked bodies as expanded and remove inactive overlay triggers from interaction; restore the single-expanded-panel behavior and button semantics on desktop.
fixes.why: Phones show every body while three triggers announce aria-expanded=false; tapping them produces no corresponding disclosure change.

fixes.what: Align paired fields at the bottom of each row and give single-line inputs a consistent height, allowing helper text above them without stretching adjacent controls.
fixes.why: The desktop screenshot shows the email input taller and starting above the names input because the two field grids contain different numbers of rows.
